english_translation: We are planning tomorrow's trip to Harare.

dialogue.shona: Tiri kuronga rwendo rwemangwana rwekuenda Harare.
dialogue.english: We are planning tomorrow's trip to Harare.
dialogue.literal_gloss: Tiri [tiri] • kuronga [to / at ronga] • rwendo [rwendo] • rwemangwana [rwemangwana] • rwekuenda [rwekuenda] • Harare [harare]

grammar_notes.title: Actions Happening Right Now: The '-ri ku-' Progressive
grammar_notes.content: To describe an action that is happening right now ('I am doing', 'it is raining', 'they are walking'), Shona uses the helper verb '-ri' ('am/is/are') followed by 'ku-' ('to') and the action verb. For people, the forms are 'ndiri ku-' (I am), 'uri ku-' (you are), 'ari ku-' (he/she is), 'tiri ku-' (we are), and 'vari ku-' (they are). In fast speech or writing, the two words are sometimes joined together (e.g., 'ndiri kuenda' or 'ndirikuenda').
grammar_notes.rule: [Subject + -ri] + ku-[verb] -> Ndiri kuverenga (I am reading) | Vari kufamba (They are walking) | Mvura iri kunaya (It is raining)

grammar_notes.title: Infinitive Verbs & Action Nouns with 'ku-' ('kuronga')
grammar_notes.content: Look at 'kuronga' in this sentence. Every Shona verb in its dictionary ('to do') form begins with 'ku-': for example, 'kudya' (to eat), 'kutenga' (to buy), 'kubhadhara' (to pay), 'kuona' (to see), and 'kurwa' (to fight). Because 'ku-' verbs also behave as action nouns ('eating', 'paying', 'working'), you can attach linking prefixes directly to them: 'yekubhadhara' ('for paying'), 'pakubikwa' ('in the cooking'), and 'nekuona' ('by/with seeing').
grammar_notes.rule: ku- + Verb Stem = 'to [verb] / [verb]-ing' (ku- + -tenga = kutenga, 'to buy'; ye- + kubhadhara = yekubhadhara, 'for paying')

grammar_notes.title: How Shona Sentences Fit Together (Subject + Tense + Verb)
grammar_notes.content: In 'Tiri kuronga rwendo rwemangwana rwekuenda Harare.', notice how a single Shona verb word packs together who is doing the action (the subject prefix), when it happens (the tense marker), and the action itself (the verb stem). Once you recognize the building blocks at the start of the verb—like 'ndi-' (I), 'u-' (you), 'ti-' (we), or 'va-' (they)—you can immediately spot the subject even when no separate pronoun word is used!
grammar_notes.rule: [Who (Subject Prefix)] + [When (Tense Marker)] + [Action (Verb Root)] -> e.g., ti- (we) + -cha- (will) + -svika (arrive) = tichasvika

cultural_notes.title: Travelling to Harare ('Guta guru reZimbabwe')
cultural_notes.content: Harare—Zimbabwe's capital and largest commercial hub, historically known as 'Harare' after Chief Neharawa—is the focal point for business, university study, and intercity travel from every province of the country.

active_exercises.prompt: How do you say 'Our journey was very good' in Shona?
active_exercises.explanation: 'Rwendo rwedu' = 'Our journey' (taking 'rw-' agreement), 'rwakanga rwakanaka kwazvo' = 'was very good'.

active_exercises.prompt: Translate this new sentence into English: 'Vanhu vakamira pamusika vachimirira kukwira bhazi.'
options: The driver stopped the car near the traffic lights.
People are standing at the market waiting to board the bus.
We saw two large trucks carrying maize to the city.
The road to the eastern highlands has many curves.
active_exercises.correct_answer: People are standing at the market waiting to board the bus.
active_exercises.explanation: 'Vanhu vakamira pamusika' = 'People are standing at the market', 'vachimirira kukwira bhazi' = 'waiting to board the bus'.

active_exercises.prompt: Why do we say 'miti mitatu' for 'three trees' but 'zvigaro zvitatu' for 'three chairs'?
options: Because trees are taller than chairs
Because 'mitatu' means thirty and 'zvitatu' means three
The number stem '-tatu' takes 'mi-' for 'miti' (trees) and 'zvi-' for 'zvigaro' (chairs)
Because 'miti' is singular and 'zvigaro' is plural
active_exercises.correct_answer: The number stem '-tatu' takes 'mi-' for 'miti' (trees) and 'zvi-' for 'zvigaro' (chairs)
active_exercises.explanation: Numbers 1–5 mirror the prefix of the noun they count: 'miti mitatu', 'zvigaro zvitatu', 'vanhu vatatu'.
